questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Because of COVID I wanted a place that was within the EU with an institution that had a good reputation and courses that were relevant to my interests. Belgium fulfilled all these requirements.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy enough. I had to do some digging on the university pages, as well as sign up for orientation days, which were very helpful

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation Days with all information that Erasmus students needed to know, organised by the University.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are plenty of dorms in Leuven that belong to KU Leuven. Most of them are very close to the KU Leuven buildings

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Plenty of options! Supermarkets like Aldi, Carrefour, Spar within walking distance, restaurants and the student restaurants called ALMA, which are affordable for students. Dorms have kitchens with all necessary appliances. No one will go hungry in Leuven

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Sent emails in advance to as many dorms as possible. If you are put on a waiting list, don't lose hope, cancellations happen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When students arrive they are instructed to go and register in one of the KU Leuven buildings as students. Then, you register for your courses online in the Toledo portal.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Instructions from Orientation Days and the academic supervisor in KU Leuven

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: That was a bit tricky. Some courses I had chosen where not available for me and I had to switch. But overall all courses were interesting so I believe it worked out in the end

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep in mind that to get 30 ECTS you need to register for 5 or 6 courses. It's a lot of coursework and exams will be difficult as a result. But if you're interested in the subjects you will have fun

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All of them where MA level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In KU Leuven the atmosphere is a bit different than UCPH. Continuous discussions in class are encouraged and sometimes the professor spends a lot of time answering questions. Classes are also bigger with more participants. Most professors are quite friendly. In some courses, students are expected to give oral presentations and answer questions about them.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Media Ethics
Husserl in Context
Metaphysics
Philosophy of Technology
East and West perspectives
Political Philosophy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It depends on someone's interest! Political philosophy is highly recommended because the professor makes the topic very engaging. Husserl in context is a must for those interested in phenomelogy, but it requires a lot of intense studying of difficult texts. Philosophy of technology deals with relevant, modern subjects. Overall all the courses I attended were interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you can, avoid coming to Leuven from Charleroi Airport, its pricey and confusing. Also be aware that Leuven is filled with delicious food in restaurants so you will spent some time there. And it's well connected so expect to be doing quite a bit of travelling

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fruit can be expensive, and for some reason meat is very pricey. Other than that, it was quite affordable

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: KU Leuven has Pangea, which is a student run cafe, very friendly to international students. There's ESN, as well for Erasmus students. There are also student clubs that you can sign up to and student teams that organise talks and events, for most of the faculties. There's a LGTBQ society, STEM societies and basically every thing you can think of!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The sports centre is free for students and there's many different training facilities and a pool. There's also a student cinema which offers discounts. Student clubs and societies organise trips, talks, parties etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the sports centre, for certain. And the discounts at Cinema Zed. There's also ice rink place near the town for ice skating .

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: , Do some travelling to Flanders, Brussels or Wallonia. Visit the restaurants and cafes in Leuven. Visit the churches and the park. There's so many things to do!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Belgians are quite friendly and helpful. There were no problems.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't miss Pangea events, particularly in the beginning. It's very easy to make friends because the town is quite small and there is a huge student population.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language. It's useful to know that Belgium is divided in two regions based on language. In Wallonia people speak French, in Flanders, people speak Dutch. Therefore, French is quite useful (and largely unwelcome) in Leuven. But in Brussels, which is 20 minutes away by train, everyone speaks French. This is something a foreigner needs to  adjust to. At least, people in Flanders speak good English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food is amazing. German portions with a  French flair. Additionally the history of Belgium is very fascinating and people can see the WW1 sites and museums dedicated to WW1. Also, Belgium is famous for its comic book tradition. And the architecture in towns is very interesting.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
E mail the dorms in advance about a room.

Note that the coursework will be challenging because you have to select a lot of courses.

Remember that you will have fun regardless.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: KU Leuven is demanding, so bare it in mind. I managed to balance socialising and studying quite well, but exams were difficult. Make sure to make friends to support you through the process. Still, it is a great experience.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made, as well as all the topics of the courses and the professors' approach. It definitely expanded my perspective as a student and as a person. I learned a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exams. But they can be beaten.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to KU Leuven, you won't regret it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
